title: RAG architecture: chunking, embedding, retrieval, reranking, grounding

claims.text: Lewis and colleagues set out the framing at the 2020 conference on neural information processing systems: large pre-trained models store factual knowledge in their parameters, but their ability to access and precisely manipulate knowledge is limited, so on knowledge-intensive tasks they lag behind task-specific architectures, and providing provenance for decisions and updating world knowledge remain open problems.

source.title: Patrick Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, pages 9459-9474, 2020 (arXiv:2005.11401)

claims.text: Their construction combines two memories: a parametric memory, which is a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence model, and a non-parametric memory, which is a dense vector index accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever, combined in a probabilistic model trained end to end. For a query, a maximum inner product search finds the top documents, which are treated as a latent variable and marginalised over.

source.title: Patrick Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, pages 9459-9474, 2020 (arXiv:2005.11401)

claims.text: Two results matter for design. On language generation the models produce more specific, diverse and factual language than a parametric-only baseline. And the world knowledge can be updated by simply replacing the non-parametric memory, which addresses the staleness that contributes to outdated-fact errors.

source.title: Patrick Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33, pages 9459-9474, 2020 (arXiv:2005.11401)

beats.broke: a model knows what was in its training data, cannot tell you where an answer came from, and cannot be corrected without retraining
beats.fix: split knowledge in two — leave language ability in the parameters and put facts in an external index that is searched at question time, so answers are grounded in retrieved text that can be cited
beats.cost: the answer is now only as good as what retrieval returned, so every failure of the retriever becomes a failure of the system, and the retriever fails silently by returning plausible but irrelevant passages
beats.interview: where a retrieval-augmented system actually fails
